subject: History
topic: Partition and Independence 1947 — Mountbatten Plan, princely states, Radcliffe Line
description: Partition of India 1947: Mountbatten Plan, Radcliffe Line, communal riots, Congress and League positions, princely states integration, Sardar Patel, Hyderabad/Junagadh/Kashmir accession.

questions.stem: The Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947) provided for the independence of India primarily by:

options.option_text: Partitioning British India into two dominions — India and Pakistan — based on Muslim-majority provinces
Granting independence to a united India as a single federation of provinces and princely states
Creating three separate nations — India, Pakistan, and Bengal — each under British protection
Transferring power jointly to Congress and Muslim League for a 5-year transition period

questions.explanation: MOUNTBATTEN PLAN (3 June Plan): announced by Lord Mountbatten (last Viceroy). KEY PROVISIONS: (1) British India partitioned into TWO dominions: India and Pakistan. (2) Muslim-majority provinces (West Punjab, Sindh, Baluchistan, NWFP, East Bengal) → Pakistan. (3) Legislatures of Punjab and Bengal to vote on partition of their own provinces. (4) Transfer of power by 15 August 1947 (advanced from June 1948). RADCLIFFE COMMISSION: drew the boundary. INDEPENDENCE AND PARTITION ACT 1947: passed by British Parliament. PYQ: Mountbatten Plan provisions in UPSC, SSC, IBPS history GK.

questions.stem: The integration of over 500 princely states into the Indian Union after independence was primarily accomplished by:

options.option_text: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, using both persuasion and firmness as first Home Minister and Deputy PM
Jawaharlal Nehru, who negotiated directly with each ruler through Parliament committees
Lord Mountbatten, who issued a directive ordering all rulers to accede before independence
The Constituent Assembly, which passed a resolution making accession mandatory for all states

questions.explanation: SARDAR PATEL: called 'Iron Man of India' and 'Bismarck of India' for integrating princely states. INSTRUMENT OF ACCESSION: standardised document signed by rulers transferring defence, foreign affairs, communications to India. VP MENON: Secretary, States Ministry — Patel's key bureaucratic aide. DIFFICULT CASES: (1) HYDERABAD: Muslim Nizam refused; India conducted Operation Polo (Police Action, Sept 1948). (2) JUNAGADH: Muslim ruler over Hindu-majority state; India held plebiscite; integrated. (3) KASHMIR: Hari Singh signed after Pakistani tribal invasion (Oct 1947). PYQ: Patel + princely states in UPSC, SSC 1-2x per cycle.

questions.stem: The Radcliffe Line, which demarcated the boundary between India and Pakistan in 1947, was drawn by:

options.option_text: Sir Cyril Radcliffe — a British lawyer who had never visited India before the assignment
Lord Mountbatten personally — he suggested the boundary as the last Viceroy of India
A joint Indo-Pak commission of elected representatives from both new nations
The British Parliament, which finalised the boundary before passing the Independence Act

questions.explanation: RADCLIFFE COMMISSION: established to demarcate boundaries for Punjab and Bengal. CHAIRMAN: Sir Cyril Radcliffe — a London barrister who had NEVER visited India. He had only 5 weeks to draw the line (June–August 1947). TWO BOUNDARIES: Punjab Boundary Commission and Bengal Boundary Commission. PUBLICATION: announced on 17 August 1947 — two days AFTER independence — creating immediate refugee crisis. CONSEQUENCES: 10-20 million refugees crossed the new borders; 200,000-2 million killed in communal violence. PYQ: Radcliffe Line + who drew it in UPSC, SSC history.

questions.stem: India's Instrument of Accession during the Kashmir crisis of 1947 was signed by:

options.option_text: Maharaja Hari Singh — the Hindu ruler of Jammu & Kashmir, signed after Pakistani tribal invasion
Sheikh Abdullah — he was the popular National Conference leader, not the ruler of the state
Lord Mountbatten — Mountbatten accepted the accession on India's behalf but did not sign it
Jawaharlal Nehru — Nehru accepted the accession but Hari Singh was the signatory ruler

questions.explanation: KASHMIR ACCESSION: October 1947. Maharaja HARI SINGH (Hindu ruler of Muslim-majority J&K) initially sought independence. CRISIS: Pakistani tribal militias (Kabalis) invaded Kashmir on 22 October 1947. Hari Singh appealed to India for military help. CONDITION: India demanded accession first. Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947. Lord Mountbatten (Governor-General) accepted on behalf of India. Indian Army airlifted into Srinagar on 27 October. UN CEASEFIRE: January 1, 1949. ARTICLE 370: special status, later abrogated in August 2019. PYQ: Kashmir accession in UPSC, SSC, IBPS GK.

questions.stem: Operation Polo (September 1948) was a military action taken by India to:

options.option_text: Integrate Hyderabad into the Indian Union — the Nizam had refused to accede after independence
Defend Kashmir against the Pakistani tribal invasion from the northwest (not this)
Annex Junagadh after its ruler had initially acceded to Pakistan (not this)
Restore order in Punjab during the communal riots following Partition (not this)

questions.explanation: OPERATION POLO (September 17-18, 1948): also called the Police Action. CONTEXT: Hyderabad was India's largest princely state; Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan refused to accede, sought independence or UN arbitration. Internal unrest (Razakars — Muslim paramilitary). Sardar Patel ordered military action. RESULT: Hyderabad integrated into India in 5 days. CONTRAST: OPERATION VIJAY (1961) = Goa annexation from Portugal. OPERATION CACTUS (1988) = India's intervention in Maldives. PYQ: Operation Polo in UPSC, SSC, state PSC modern history.

questions.stem: The Two-Nation Theory, the ideological basis for Pakistan's creation, was most prominently advocated by:

options.option_text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah — he argued Hindus and Muslims were two separate nations requiring separate homelands
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan — he promoted Muslim education and cooperation with the British, not partition
Allama Iqbal — he proposed a Muslim homeland in the northwest but within an Indian federation
Liaquat Ali Khan — he was Jinnah's key deputy; the theory itself preceded his rise to prominence

questions.explanation: TWO-NATION THEORY: Jinnah's central argument — Hindus and Muslims are two distinct nations with different religions, cultures, history, customs; cannot coexist peacefully in a single state. LAHORE RESOLUTION 1940: Muslim League formally demanded separate states for Muslim-majority areas. IQBAL'S CONTRIBUTION (1930): proposed a consolidated North-West Indian Muslim state — but within or alongside India; not the same as Jinnah's demand for a fully separate Pakistan. SIR SYED AHMAD KHAN: 19th century; founded AMU; believed Muslims should cooperate with British — intellectual forerunner but not the same theory. PYQ: Two-Nation Theory + Jinnah in UPSC, SSC modern history.

questions.stem: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) proposed which solution for Indian independence that was ultimately rejected?

options.option_text: A three-tier federal structure — Union, Provinces, and Groups — with Muslims and Hindus in separate province groups
An immediate division of India into three separate nations — India, Pakistan, and a neutral Bengal
A dominion status for 15 years followed by full independence after a review period (not this)
A joint British-Indian condominium to govern India for 10 years before transfer of power (not this)

questions.explanation: CABINET MISSION (1946): sent by PM Attlee. Members: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander. PLAN: (1) United India (no partition). (2) Three-tier federation: Union (defence/foreign affairs), Groups of provinces (A=Hindu-majority, B=Muslim-majority NW, C=Bengal+Assam), Individual provinces. (3) ML could have autonomous control within groups without Pakistan. FAILURE: Nehru's statement that Congress would not be bound by groupings → ML withdrew acceptance → Direct Action Day (August 1946 riots). SIGNIFICANCE: the last serious attempt to keep India united. Led directly to Mountbatten Plan. PYQ: Cabinet Mission plan in UPSC Prelims/Mains, SSC.
